US-119-HR8195.title: Responsible Cormorant Management and Control Act of 2026
US-119-HR8195.summary:
Responsible Cormorant Management and Control Act of 2026

This bill requires the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) to develop frameworks to manage regional populations of double-crested cormorants (a type of waterbird native to North America).

Specifically, FWS must coordinate with the four Regional Flyway Councils to develop regional management frameworks for double-crested cormorants. Among other elements, each framework must (1) ensure the breeding population is managed at a sufficient level to ensure conservation, (2) include parameters regarding the taking (e.g., capturing or hunting) of double-crested cormorants, and (3) consider any documented effects of double-crested cormorants in the region (e.g., impacts on fisheries).

In developing each framework, FWS must also work with state and tribal game and fish agencies and the applicable Regional Flyway Council to make recommendations for managing double-crested cormorants within the National Wildlife Refuge System.

FWS must coordinate with the Regional Flyway Councils every five years to survey the population of double-crested cormorants. Additionally, each framework must be reviewed and updated every five years, incorporating results of the most recent population survey. FWS must also report to Congress on the feasibility of issuing hunting licenses to manage double-crested cormorants in accordance with the frameworks.

The requirements of this bill terminate on January 1, 2034.

US-119-HR8195.aiSummary: The bill would require the Interior Secretary to create regional plans for managing double-crested cormorants, working with flyway councils, states, and tribes. The plans would set rules for when and how the birds may be taken, require public yearly reports, and call for nonlethal steps and habitat fixes. It would also require bird population surveys every 5 years, updates to the plans every 5 years, and would end on January 1, 2034.

US-119-HR10790.title: Chemical Safety Board Accountability Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10790.description: To amend the Clean Air Act to require that at least one member of the Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board has demonstrated knowledge and substantial experience in the trades or industrial labor, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10790.aiSummary: The bill would change the rules for the Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board. It would require at least one board member to have experience in trades or industrial labor, and it would also set rules for filling vacancies, removing members, and the chair’s role. It affects the board’s members and presidential nominations.

US-119-HR10691.description: To prohibit the use of automatic license plate readers by the Federal Government without explicit statutory authorization, to withhold grants awarded by certain agencies from State and local governments that use automatic license plate readers, and to prohibit the use of Federal funds to purchase automatic license plate readers.
US-119-HR10691.aiSummary: The bill would bar the federal government from using automatic license plate readers, except where another law clearly allows it, and would also ban federal funds from being used to buy or use them. It would cut certain grants to state and local governments unless they already have a law or policy that bans these readers to the same or a greater degree. It also sets rules for toll use, data retention, and penalties for violations.

US-119-HR9086.title: Foreign Service Modernization Act
US-119-HR9086.summary:
Foreign Service Modernization Act

This bill requires or authorizes certain actions related to U.S. Foreign Service (FS) management and operations, including an increased focus on expeditionary diplomacy (a concept that emphasizes diplomats conducting direct diplomacy in high-risk environments outside of the embassy), expanded hiring pathways, and additional training requirements.

For example, the bill requires the Department of State to establish
• a team to develop a plan to improve the capability and willingness of FS members and leaders to engage in expeditionary diplomacy;
• a program to recruit qualified veterans and separating military personnel into the FS, including by integrating FS recruitment into military transition programs; and
• a Diplomatic Reserve Corps pilot program to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of a trained reserve cadre providing a surge workforce to support foreign affairs contingencies.

Additionally, the State Department is authorized to establish a structured training framework that is integrated into normal career progression with protected training periods (similar to the Armed Forces' professional military education model).

The bill specifies that FS members
• must successfully complete specified leadership and management training prior to assuming leadership assignments;
• who participate in approved external training, education, or details shall have certain employment protections (such as eligibility for promotions and pay increases on the same basis as those not on such assignments); and
• who undergo full-time, department-funded language training for more than six months must serve at least three consecutive tours in positions requiring proficiency in that language, with assignments beginning immediately after such language training.

US-119-HR9086.aiSummary: The bill would change how the State Department manages and trains U.S. Foreign Service members. It would create new programs for expeditionary diplomacy, veteran and military hiring, and a reserve corps pilot program, and it would add training and job rules for some Foreign Service staff. It would also give some workers protections while they take approved outside training, education, or work details.

US-119-HR10394.title: Protecting Approved Care Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10394.description: To amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to establish requirements with respect to the use of prior authorization and claims denial under Medicare Advantage plans.
US-119-HR10394.aiSummary: The bill would set new rules for Medicare Advantage plans on prior approval and claim denials. Starting with plan years on or after January 1, 2028, if a plan approves care, or if care does not need prior approval, the plan could not later deny it for lack of medical need, reopen the decision in most cases, or change the claim code to cut payment. These rules would affect Medicare Advantage plans and people enrolled in them.

US-119-HR10350.title: Protecting Elders from Wire Fraud Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10350.description: To protect elders from wire fraud by imposing requirements on covered financial institutions, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10350.aiSummary: The bill would require certain financial firms to report suspected financial abuse of seniors within 5 days and send key details about the person and the suspected abuse. It would also let the firm put a hold on a suspicious transaction for up to 30 business days, with possible 30-day extensions, and tell a trusted contact when appropriate. The changes would take effect 180 days after enactment.

US-119-HR10273.title: Fairness for Farm Workers Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10273.description: To amend the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to provide increased labor law protections for agricultural workers, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10273.aiSummary: The bill would change federal wage rules for farm workers by adding overtime pay after set weekly hours, with the hours phasing down from 55 to 40 over several years. It would also remove some current farm work exceptions in labor law and change family-work and small-farm rules. The changes would apply at different times based on employer size, with smaller employers getting later start dates.

US-119-HR10174.title: GRANITE Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10174.description: To amend title 28, United States Code, to limit the enforcement of foreign censorship judgments, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10174.aiSummary: The bill would stop U.S. courts from enforcing certain foreign court judgments, fines, orders, or demands that are tied to foreign censorship laws. It would also let a U.S. person ask a federal court to rule that such a judgment cannot be enforced here. The bill defines foreign censorship laws as foreign laws that restrict or punish speech or force disclosure in ways that would conflict with First Amendment protections.
